body.p: By this response, claims 1, 3-17, and 19-22 are pending. Claims 1, 3, 10, 11, and 17 are amended. Claims 2 and 18 are canceled. Claims 21 and 22 are newly added. No new subject matter is added.
I. Rejections Under 35 U.S.C. & 102 and 103

Claims 1-3, 5, 11-14, and 17-19 are rejected are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(1) as being anticipated by Vallart et al. US 20160327958 ("Vallart"). Claims 4, 15, and 20 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over Vallart in view of Romana et al. US 20170008619 ("Romana"). Claims 6-8 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over Vallart in view of White EP 3208190 ("White"). Claims 9-10 and 16 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over Vallart in view of Waltner et al. US 20180305038 ("Waltner").
a. Independent Claim 1

Amended independent claim 1 recites a control system for an aircraft including, among other things, a controller configured to receive the pilot input via the pilot input device, receive a sensed force on the landing gear via the first sensor, calculate an output command based at least on the pilot input and the force on the landing gear, wherein the controller calculates the output command by calculating a correction factor based on the pilot input and the sensed force on the landing gear, and transmit the output command to control the aircraft.

Claim 1 is amended to include the subject matter of dependent claim 2 in order to clarify that the controller calculates the output command by calculating a correction factor based on the pilot input and the sensed force on the landing gear. The Examiner rejects independent claim 1 and dependent claim 2 as being anticipated by Vallart. Applicant respectfully disagrees.
Vallart fails to teach or suggest calculating a correction factor based, at least in part, on

the sensed force of the landing gear. Rather, Vallart uses force sensors merely for the purpose of identifying whether the rotocraft is in an "in flight" state or a "touching" state. However, once the state of the rotocraft is identified, there is no indication that the information obtained from the sensors is used to calculate a correction factor. More specifically, Vallart discloses a control

system for a rotocraft, which includes a means for detecting a ground reaction force F1, F2, F3 exerted on the landing gear for the purpose of identifying the state of the rotocraft between an "in flight" state and a "touching" state. Vallart [0038]-[0040. The "touching" state is identified when the following two conditions are met: 1) the reaction force F 1 is greater than the low threshold (SH) value but lower than the high threshold (SH) value; and 2) each of the reaction forces F2 and F3 is lower than the low threshold (Ss) value. Vallart [0041]-[0043]. The "in flight" state is identified when each of the reaction forces F1, F2, F3 is lower than the low threshold (Ss) value. Vallart [0044]. Once the controller determines which flight state the rotocraft is in, it is able to determine which control logic should be implemented. A first control law is implemented when the rotorcraft is in an "in flight" state, and a second control law is implemented when the rotocraft is in a "touching" state. Vallart [0046]-[0047]. In other words, the reaction forces F1, F2, F3 are used to determine which flight state the rotocraft is in, and thus, which control laws to use depending on the state.
Accordingly, Vallart discloses the use of sensors on the landing gear solely for the
purpose of determining a flight state of the rotocraft. However, Vallart fails to teach or suggest utilizing sensors on the landing gear to calculate a correction factor.

None of the other cited references cure the deficiency of Vallart because none of the cited references teaches or suggests calculating a correction factor based on the pilot input and the sensed forces on the landing gear, as required by claim 1. Specifically, none of the cited references teaches or suggests utilizing force sensors on the landing gear to calculate a correction factor. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully submits that claim 1 is allowable over the prior art.
Claims 3-10 and 21-22 ultimately depend from claim 1 and are allowable for at least these reasons, in addition to independent reasons not discussed herein.
b. Independent Claim 11

Amended independent claim 11 recites a method of controlling an aircraft including, among other things, receiving a pilot input including a setpoint, receiving a first signal from a first sensor positioned on a landing gear of the aircraft, and calculating a first correction factor based on the setpoint and the first signal.
The Examiner rejects independent claim 11 as being anticipated by Vallart. Applicant respectfully disagrees. As explained in further detail above with respect to claim 1, Vallart fails

to teach or suggest calculating a correction factor based, at least in part, on the sensed force of the landing gear. Rather, Vallart uses force sensors merely for the purpose of identifying whether the rotocraft is in an "in flight" state or a "touching" state. Accordingly, Vallart discloses the use of sensors on the landing gear solely for the purpose of determining a flight state of the rotocraft. However, Vallart fails to teach or suggest utilizing sensors on the landing gear to calculate a correction factor.

None of the other cited references cure the deficiency of Vallart. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully submits that claim 11 is allowable over the prior art. Claims 12-16 ultimately depend from claim 11 and are allowable for at least these reasons, in addition to independent reasons not discussed herein.
c. Independent Claim 17

Amended independent claim 17 recites a control system for an aircraft including, among other things, a plurality of sensors positioned on a corresponding landing gear of the aircraft and configured to sense a parameter on the corresponding landing gear, and a configured to calculate an output command based on the pilot input and the sensed parameters of the landing gear, wherein the controller calculates the output command by calculating a correction factor based on the pilot input and the sensed parameters on the landing gear.
Claim 17 is amended to include the subject matter of dependent claim 18 in order to

clarify that the controller calculates the output command by calculating a correction factor based on the pilot input and the sensed force on the landing gear. The Examiner rejects independent claim 17 and dependent claim 18 as being anticipated by Vallart. Applicant respectfully disagrees.
The Examiner rejects independent claim 17 as being anticipated by Vallart. Applicant

respectfully disagrees. As explained in further detail above with respect to claim 1, Vallart fails to teach or suggest calculating a correction factor based, at least in part, on the sensed force of the landing gear. Rather, Vallart uses force sensors merely for the purpose of identifying whether the rotocraft is in an "in flight" state or a "touching" state. Accordingly, Vallart discloses the use of sensors on the landing gear solely for the purpose of determining a flight state of the rotocraft. However, Vallart fails to teach or suggest utilizing sensors on the landing gear to calculate a correction factor.

None of the other cited references cure the deficiency of Vallart. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully submits that claim 17 is allowable over the prior art. Claims 19-20 ultimately depend from claim 17 and are allowable for at least these reasons, in addition to independent reasons not discussed herein.
d. Dependent Claims

As mentioned above, each of the dependent claims is patentable for individual reasons not specifically discussed herein. For the sake of brevity, Applicant has focused the present remarks on the independent claims. However, it should be noted that Applicant contends that the prior art does not teach, suggest, or render obvious any of the subject matter recited in dependent claims 3-10, 12-16, or 19-22.
II. Conclusion

In view of the amendments and remarks presented herein, it is respectfully submitted that the claims are in condition for allowance. Therefore, Applicant requests withdrawal of the present rejections and/or objections in order to allow the application to be allowed. Applicant requests that the Examiner telephone the attorneys or agents of record in the event a telephone discussion would be helpful in advancing the prosecution of this application.
